headline: Epitalon
punch: The one with a mechanism that gets worse the longer you run it.

headline: What it actually is
body: **Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly**, a four residue synthetic peptide, developed as the active analogue of Epithalamin, the original bovine pineal extract. | Its headline mechanism is telomerase activation. It extends telomere length in normal human cell lines by upregulating **hTERT**, which is the one claim in this family that is both specific and testable.
punch: A four amino acid telomerase activator.

headline: It is far stronger
body: Same-study, same-species head to head comparisons put Epitalon at roughly **100 to 1000 times** the potency of Epithalamin. | In rhesus monkeys, **10 µg per animal per day of Epitalon matched 5 mg per animal per day of Epithalamin**, a 500-fold gap. In an antioxidant assay Epithalamin was dosed 1000 times higher and was still the weaker compound. Primate dose data is rare in this family.

headline: Telomerase is pro-growth
body: If it genuinely extends the replicative capacity of a progenitor pool, that is mechanistically pro-growth in a tissue whose limit is replicative exhaustion. | Growth plate closure is driven by the resting zone running out of divisions. A compound that raises telomerase in that compartment is at least pointed at the right constraint, which is more than most of this family manages.

headline: The cancer cell finding
body: Epitalon extends telomeres in normal cells via hTERT. In **breast cancer cell lines 21NT and BT474** it does it by a different route, **alternative lengthening of telomeres**, and it does so **dose-dependently**. | This is described as the single mechanism in this compound family that **plausibly scales worst with duration and dose of exposure**. Note also that this paper carries a published correction.
punch: ==A telomere mechanism active in cancer lines, dose-dependently.==

headline: Estrogen cuts both ways
body: Epitalon is also claimed to regulate estradiol and the pineal-pituitary-thyroid axis. For height that is **directionally ambiguous**, and ambiguous is the problem. | Estrogen is the fusion signal. A compound that moves estradiol in an unspecified direction, in someone trying to keep plates open, could be helping or could be closing them faster. **No data resolves this either way.**
punch: It moves the fusion hormone. Nobody knows which way.

headline: It conflicts with senolytics
body: Epitalon prevents cells becoming senescent; FOXO4-DRI kills cells that already are. Those are not directly contradictory on their own terms. | But in the growth plate the combination has an unpredictable net effect, because **chondrocyte senescence is part of the normal endochondral ossification programme**. Suppressing and clearing senescence in a tissue that uses senescence as a step is not obviously additive in either direction.
punch: The plate uses senescence on purpose.

headline: No growing-animal data
body: Like the rest of the family, Epitalon has **zero direct evidence in a growing animal or on craniofacial tissue**. All claimed relevance is extrapolated from adult, aged or ovariectomised models. | And its human dosing follows the family tradition of pulsed 10 to 30 day courses, with the longest documented programme being Epithalamin given as 6 courses over 3 years.
punch: Nothing measured in anything still growing.

headline: The mechanism is disputed
body: The claim that a four residue peptide binds DNA with sequence specificity is considered biologically implausible, since conventional transcription factors need 30 to 60 or more residues for that. | No independent laboratory has replicated the core mechanism, and the efficacy literature has not been replicated outside Russia.

headline: Short courses, not daily
subhead: COUNTER · WHAT THE TRADITION ACTUALLY IS
body: If you run it, the documented pattern is pulsed courses of 10 to 30 days with long gaps, not continuous daily use. Every human regimen located across this family follows that shape. | Given that the one concerning mechanism is explicitly **dose and duration dependent**, the traditional pulsed schedule happens to be the right shape for the risk, whether or not that was the reason for it.
punch: The dose-dependent risk argues for the pulsed course.

headline: Verdict
body: The most specific and testable mechanism in its family, with rare primate dose data and a clear potency ratio against its parent compound. It is also the only one with a mechanism that gets more concerning with more exposure. | No growing-animal data, an ambiguous effect on the hormone that closes plates, and an unreplicated core mechanism. If used at all, the short pulsed course is the defensible shape.
punch: Real mechanism. Wrong direction risk. Keep it short.
